prompt_text:
Task: Managed Metrics Monitoring

Write code that compares metric values for two resources or dimension filters over the same window using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Azure Monitor Metrics:
  Service: Azure Monitor Metrics
  SDK: azure-monitor-query
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: query_resource, list_metric_namespaces, list_metric_definitions
  Setup hints: AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/essentials/data-platform-metrics, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/python/api/overview/azure/monitor-querymetrics-readme

Option 2 — Amazon CloudWatch Metrics:
  Service: Amazon CloudWatch Metrics
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: get_metric_data, get_metric_statistics, list_metrics
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/APIReference/API_GetMetricData.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/APIReference/API_ListMetrics.html

Option 3 — Alibaba CloudMonitor:
  Service: CloudMonitor
  SDK: alibabacloud_cms20190101 / Tea
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: DescribeMetricList, DescribeCustomMetricList
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET, ALIBABA_CLOUD_REGION_ID
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2513241.html, https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2513233.html

Option 4 — IBM Cloud Monitoring:
  Service: IBM Cloud Monitoring
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: POST /data, metric filters, aggregation expressions
  Setup hints: IBM_CLOUD_API_KEY, IBM_MONITORING_INSTANCE_ID, IBM_MONITORING_ENDPOINT
  Official docs: https://www.ibm.com/products/cloud-monitoring

Option 5 — Google Cloud Monitoring:
  Service: Cloud Monitoring
  SDK: google-cloud-monitoring
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: list_time_series, list_metric_descriptors
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/ref_v3/rest/v3/projects.timeSeries/list, https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/ref_v3/rest/v3/projects.metricDescriptors/list

Option 6 — Datadog:
  Service: Datadog Metrics API
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: submit_metrics, query_timeseries_points
  Setup hints: DD_API_KEY, DD_APP_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.datadoghq.com/metrics/custom_metrics/, https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/metrics/

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import os
import datetime
from azure.monitor.query import MetricsQueryClient
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

def compare_metrics(
    resource_uri: str,
    metric_name: str,
    time_grain: datetime.timedelta,
    duration: datetime.timedelta,
    filter_1: str,
    filter_2: str,
    aggregation: str = "Average",
) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
    """
    Compares the average value of a metric for two different filters on the same resource
    over a specified time window using Azure Monitor.

    Args:
        resource_uri: The ARM ID of the Azure resource.
                      Example: "/subscriptions/<subid>/resourceGroups/<rgname>/providers/<provider>/<resourcetype>/<resourcename>"
        metric_name: The name of the metric to query (e.g., "BytesReceived").
        time_grain: The granularity of the metric data (e.g., datetime.timedelta(minutes=5)).
        duration: The time duration for which to retrieve the metric data
                  (e.g., datetime.timedelta(hours=1)).
        filter_1: The OData filter expression for the first comparison.
                  Example: "Instance eq 'vm1'"
        filter_2: The OData filter expression for the second comparison.
                  Example: "Instance eq 'vm2'"
        aggregation: The aggregation type (e.g., "Average", "Minimum", "Maximum", "Total", "Count").

    Returns:
        A tuple containing the aggregated value for filter_1 and filter_2 respectively.
        Returns (None, None) if data is not available for either filter or metric.
    """
    credential = DefaultAzureCredential()
    client = MetricsQueryClient(credential)

    ends_on = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
    starts_on = ends_on - duration

    # Query for the first filter
    metrics_result_1 = client.query_resource(
        resource_uri=resource_uri,
        metric_names=[metric_name],
        timespan=(starts_on, ends_on),
        granularity=time_grain,
        aggregations=[aggregation],
        filter=filter_1,
        # Default top is 100, orderby is asc. For simple average comparison, these are usually fine.
        # We expect a single time series per filter with the given aggregation.
    )

    value_1 = None
    for metric in metrics_result_1.metrics:
        if metric.name == metric_name:
            for time_series in metric.time_series:
                for data_point in time_series.data:
                    # Assuming we want the average of the aggregated values
                    # For a simple comparison, we'll take the first available data point's aggregation
                    # Or sum them up and divide by count if there are multiple data points
                    # For a single 'Average' aggregation over the entire duration, Azure Monitor
                    # will return one data point per time_grain. If we want a single total average
                    # over the *entire* duration, we would sum up all 'Average' data points
                    # and divide by their count, or change the query slightly.
                    # For this task, we'll simplify and just get the average of the averages.
                    # A more robust solution might require re-aggregation of the points.
                    # Or, if only a single point is expected (e.g., if granularity is the same as duration),
                    # we take that.
                    if aggregation.lower() == "average":
                        if hasattr(data_point, "average") and data_point.average is not None:
                            if value_1 is None:
                                value_1 = 0.0
                            value_1 += data_point.average
                    elif aggregation.lower() == "total":
                        if hasattr(data_point, "total") and data_point.total is not None:
                            if value_1 is None:
                                value_1 = 0.0
                            value_1 += data_point.total
                    # Add other aggregations as needed (Min, Max, Count)
                if value_1 is not None and time_series.data:
                    # If we summed multiple data points, average them
                    if aggregation.lower() == "average":
                        value_1 /= len(time_series.data)
                    break # Assuming one time series per filter and metric for simplicity

    # Query for the second filter
    metrics_result_2 = client.query_resource(
        resource_uri=resource_uri,
        metric_names=[metric_name],
        timespan=(starts_on, ends_on),
        granularity=time_grain,
        aggregations=[aggregation],
        filter=filter_2,
    )

    value_2 = None
    for metric in metrics_result_2.metrics:
        if metric.name == metric_name:
            for time_series in metric.time_series:
                for data_point in time_series.data:
                    if aggregation.lower() == "average":
                        if hasattr(data_point, "average") and data_point.average is not None:
                            if value_2 is None:
                                value_2 = 0.0
                            value_2 += data_point.average
                    elif aggregation.lower() == "total":
                        if hasattr(data_point, "total") and data_point.total is not None:
                            if value_2 is None:
                                value_2 = 0.0
                            value_2 += data_point.total
                if value_2 is not None and time_series.data:
                    if aggregation.lower() == "average":
                        value_2 /= len(time_series.data)
                    break

    return value_1, value_2
